title: feat(mcp): bound read_file PDF and Word extraction with a CPU-time budget and a concurrency cap
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi99XugaEoa4TxLNdVNZx3ZEP)_
Fixes #31826

Clause-②: yes — `read_file` gains a new truncated answer (out of CPU budget) and a new retryable refusal (over the concurrency cap) on a door that used to answer every file within its caps in full. Not `(narrowing)`: no input it accepted is now refused for good; the refusal is transient and retryable, the truncated answer is the shape the door already serves at its length and page caps, and under the defaults every file within those caps reads as before (measured below).
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：AI 助手用 `read_file` 读 PDF / Word 时，每个文件最多耗 2 秒 CPU(到点停，返回已读部分并提示下载);同一进程最多同时抽取 4 个，再来一个立刻回「稍后再试」。两个数都由宿主环境变量设置。
- 为什么改：抽取在请求线程上同步跑，期间同进程所有别的请求都在等;共享云上一个租户连读大文件会拖慢所有人(#31100 裁定 B 第一期)。
- 风险与回滚：默认值下实测的最重文件(9 MiB、200 页)仍完整读出，行为不变;只动 `@objectstack/mcp`,回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/mcp/src/file-content.ts` 的 `withExtractionSlot` 与两处预算检查;`mcp-http-tools.ts` 的拒绝渲染;`plugin.ts` 的启动读取。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp exec vitest run src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts`,应见 28 个用例全绿，其中 7 个是新加的预算与并发用例。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地;合并后 cloud 车道在部署配置里设共享云的两个值。

## What changes

`packages/mcp/src/file-content.ts`:

- **CPU-time budget per extraction** (`OS_MCP_READ_FILE_CPU_BUDGET_MS`, default `2000`). Process CPU time, read as `process.cpuUsage()` deltas from the extraction's start (ADR-0102 D1's dimension). PDF: checked between pages, never mid-page; the first page is always read. Word: checked between paragraphs of `word/document.xml`, every 64 paragraphs (the clock read stays a rounding error on a long body); the body's single `inflateRawSync` cannot stop part-way and stays bounded by the existing 32 MiB cap. Out of budget the answer is the text read so far, `truncated: true`, and a `note`: "Reading stopped at the CPU-time budget for one file (N ms) after page K of M, so the text is partial. Download the file with the link for the rest." No new answer key: `truncated` and `note` are the keys the length and page caps already use. No wall-clock ceiling was added (the ruling makes it optional; extraction does no I/O wait a wall bound would catch).
- **Process-wide concurrency cap** (`OS_MCP_READ_FILE_MAX_CONCURRENT`, default `4`) on PDF and Word extractions in flight; text files and images are not counted. A counter taken before the extraction's first await and released in `finally`. Over the cap the call is refused at once, never queued: `ReadFileExtractionBusyError`, code `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, status `503`, message "…Try again in about N seconds."
- **Both read once at boot**: `configureReadFileExtraction()` is called from `MCPServerPlugin.init` (**boot site: `packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts`**). A value that is not a positive integer throws, naming the variable, so the boot fails (the reader follows `@objectstack/types`' `query-read-limits.ts` `readLimitVar`, the nearest loud `OS_*` numeric reader). A process that never calls it reads the host's values on its first `read_file`, outside the extractors' catch-all, so a malformed value still answers naming the variable.

`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`: the `read_file` door renders the busy refusal through the same `codedErrorResult` the other coded refusals use, with `details: { retryAfterSeconds }` (the slot the runtime's inbound rate limiter carries the wait in; a tool result has no `Retry-After` header). Every other throw keeps `errorResultWithCode`.

`content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`: both variables, their defaults and why, under "Files: `read_file` and `create_upload_link`".

## Why

#31100 ruling B (6708423049), phase 1. Phase 2 (extraction off the request thread, #31828) is not in this PR.

## Tests

New top-level `describe` in `packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts` (the file tools' shared harness), plus one boot pin in `src/__tests__/plugin.test.ts`. No existing test was edited.

- the two variables: unset → defaults; `' 750 '` / `'2'` taken; `0`, `-5`, `1.5`, `abc`, `2s` throw naming the variable.
- **CONTROL**: under the defaults a 3-page PDF and a 2-paragraph `.docx` read in full, no `truncated`, no `note`.
- PDF out of budget (a stepping CPU clock, 1 ms per read, budget 1 ms): page 1 only, `truncated: true`, the note verbatim, link present.
- Word out of budget: 200 paragraphs, stops after 64, text equals the first 64.
- Over the cap (2 held open by a pass-through `unpdf` mock): the door answers `{ code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', status: 503, message, details: { retryAfterSeconds: 3 } }`; a text file still reads; the held two finish and a slot is free again.
- N run, the N+1th is refused (cap 3, four extractions); a `.docx` is refused the same way when the one slot is held.
- an extraction that throws (the CPU clock throws at start) releases its slot: with cap 1, the next call reads.
- plugin `init` with `OS_MCP_READ_FILE_MAX_CONCURRENT=four` rejects naming the variable and registers nothing.

<details><summary>Ablations (each mutation landed on disk via scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, test red, restored to HEAD blob)</summary>

Tests import `./file-content.js` and `./mcp-http-tools.js` from `src` (no dist leg).

| # | Mutation | Red |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 | PDF budget check `if (n > 1 && budget.spent())` → `if (false)` | "a PDF out of CPU budget…" (reads all 3 pages) · 1 failed / 27 |
| A2 | Word budget check → `if (false)` | "a Word document out of CPU budget…" · 1 failed / 27 |
| A3 | cap check `if (extractionsInFlight >= limits.maxConcurrent)` → `if (false)` | "one extraction over the cap…" (the call queues behind the held two: timeout) and "N run, the N+1th is refused" (received `{ content }`, expected the busy error) · 2 failed / 26 |
| A4 | release moved out of `finally` | "an extraction that throws releases its slot" · 1 failed / 27 |
| A5 | door's busy branch → `if (false)` | "one extraction over the cap…": `details.retryAfterSeconds` missing · 1 failed / 27 |

Every leg: `ok mutation landed: anchor 1 -> 0`, then `ok restored: blob == HEAD and git diff HEAD is empty`.
</details>

<details><summary>Measurement (card item 1): a 9.21 MiB, 200-page PDF, 2,250 path operators per page, 4-core container</summary>

Method from #31100: a 1 ms `setInterval` counted during `extractFileContent`, three runs after one warm-up.

Before, `main` `4ed20928`:

```
run 1: cpu 646 ms · wall 469 ms · 1ms ticks fired 0 (missed ≈ 469)
run 2: cpu 470 ms · wall 425 ms · 1ms ticks fired 0 (missed ≈ 425)
run 3: cpu 316 ms · wall 309 ms · 1ms ticks fired 0 (missed ≈ 309)
```

After, `bd107fb4`, default budget (2000 ms): unchanged, the whole file read (8,290 chars, `truncated: false`):

```
run 1: cpu 694 ms · wall 525 ms · 1ms ticks fired 0
run 2: cpu 402 ms · wall 342 ms · 1ms ticks fired 0
run 3: cpu 286 ms · wall 279 ms · 1ms ticks fired 0
```

After, budget 100 ms: the hold is bounded by the budget.

```
run 1: cpu 106 ms · wall 50 ms · ticks fired 0 (missed ≈ 49) · truncated after page 6 of 200
run 2: cpu 103 ms · wall 36 ms · ticks fired 0 (missed ≈ 36) · truncated after page 6 of 200
run 3: cpu 101 ms · wall 78 ms · ticks fired 0 (missed ≈ 78) · truncated after page 35 of 200
```

Reading: the timer still never fires during an extraction (phase 1 bounds the hold, phase 2 removes it). Process CPU runs ahead of wall time because it also counts V8's helper threads, so the budget stops early, never late, as ADR-0102 D1 accepts.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Process CPU charges an extraction for anything interleaved with it (another extraction's microtasks, GC threads). The error direction is stopping early.
- A between-pages macrotask yield would let other requests run between pages; it is not in this card (the ruling's phase 2 moves extraction off the thread) and is listed in the report's open questions.
- The busy refusal's code is the standard `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, not a registered extension code: registering one is a `packages/spec` ledger edit, outside this card's surface. Listed in the report's open questions.
